title: Australia Awards Africa: how to prepare for the round opening 1 February 2027
description: Australia Awards pays for a full master's degree in Australia for African professionals. The next round opens on 1 February 2027. Here's who can apply, what it covers and how to get ready now.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Master's at an Australian university

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Citizens of 25 African countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Zimbabwe and Zambia

facts.label: Next round
facts.value: Opens 1 February 2027 (the last round closed on 30 April)

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: Full tuition, flights, living costs, health cover and an arrival allowance

body:
Australia Awards is one of the few fully funded scholarships built for working professionals in Africa. It pays for a full master’s degree in Australia, and it’s open to citizens of all six countries we cover.

The next application round opens on 1 February 2027. The last round ran from 1 February to 30 April 2026, so expect a window of about three months. The best applicants start preparing now.

Who can apply

These are the rules from the last round (for study starting in 2027). Check the new profile when the round opens, as details can change.

  • Citizenship: you’re a citizen of an eligible country and apply from that country. The 25 countries include Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Zimbabwe and Zambia.
  • Age: at least 25 years old on 1 February of the year your study starts.
  • Work experience: at least 5 years’ work experience after your first degree, in a field related to what you want to study, and you’re employed when you apply.
  • Education: you have a bachelor’s degree, and you don’t already have (or aren’t studying for) a master’s.
  • English: IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, or the same level in TOEFL or PTE, valid on 1 January of the year you start. There’s an exemption if English is your first language and you studied in English.
  • Previous awards: you haven’t had a long-term Australia Award before.

What it covers

  • Full tuition fees
  • Return flights
  • A contribution to living costs
  • A one-off allowance when you arrive
  • Overseas Student Health Cover
  • An introductory academic programme and extra academic support
  • Fieldwork costs for research and some coursework master’s

Australia Awards scholars must leave Australia when they finish and spend at least two years outside it, so the scholarship suits people who want to use the degree at home.

Priority study areas

The last round prioritised:

  • agriculture and food security
  • climate change
  • foreign policy and international security
  • gender, disability and social inclusion
  • mining and energy

Your application is stronger when your course and your plan clearly fit one of these.

Get ready now: a timeline

WhenWhat to do
November to December 2026Take IELTS if you need it (IELTS fees in Nigeria). Choose 2 or 3 courses in Australia.
December 2026 to January 2027Get certified copies of your degree and transcripts. Ask your employer for a letter that confirms your role and dates.
January 2027Draft your answers about your work, the course and your plan after it. See how to write a strong statement.
1 February 2027The round opens. Read the new profile and apply online through OASIS.
Before the deadlineSubmit early. Late applications aren’t considered.

If you’re shortlisted, you’ll be invited to an interview.

Other options

If you don’t have 5 years’ experience yet, look at awards with lower experience rules in our 2027 scholarship calendar, such as Gates Cambridge or Erasmus Mundus.

Australia Awards is free to apply for. Never pay anyone who promises to get you selected.

title: Duolingo English Test or IELTS: which should you take in 2026?
description: The Duolingo English Test costs $70 and you take it at home, but many visas don't accept it. Here's where it works, where you need IELTS, and how to choose.

facts.label: Duolingo English Test
facts.value: US$70, about 1 hour, taken at home, valid 2 years

facts.label: IELTS in Nigeria
facts.value: ₦299,000 for Academic or General Training

facts.label: Rule of thumb
facts.value: Duolingo for admission only; IELTS if you'll need a visa or work permit that names it

body:
The Duolingo English Test is cheaper and easier to book than IELTS, so many students ask if they can skip IELTS completely. The honest answer: sometimes. It depends on whether you only need a university admission, or also a visa that names its own list of English tests.

The two tests at a glance

Duolingo English TestIELTS
PriceUS$70₦299,000 in Nigeria (see current fees)
Where you take itAt home, on your own computerAt a test centre
LengthAbout 1 hourAbout 2 hours 45 minutes in total, including speaking
ResultsUsually within 2 daysA few days on computer, about 13 days on paper
Score10 to 160Band 1 to 9
Valid for2 years2 years for most universities and visas

Where the Duolingo English Test works

  • Many universities. A large number of universities accept it for admission, including many in the USA, Canada and Ireland, and some in the UK. Always check your course page, because some universities and courses don’t.
  • US student visas (F-1). There’s no single US government list: your university sets the English requirement for your I-20.
  • Canadian study permits. IRCC doesn’t name a language test for most study permits, so the university’s requirement is what counts.
  • Irish study visas. Ireland lists it among the English tests it accepts for study visas.

Where you need IELTS (or another approved test)

  • UK visas that need a SELT. The Duolingo English Test isn’t a UK Secure English Language Test. You can’t use it for a Skilled Worker or Health and Care visa, or for study below degree level. For a degree, your university may assess your English itself and accept it, but only if that university says so.
  • Canada Express Entry and permanent residence. IRCC only accepts CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training or PTE Core for English. Note that IELTS Academic doesn’t count here.
  • Australia and New Zealand visas. Neither accepts tests taken at home.
  • Nursing registration. The UK’s NMC and Ireland’s NMBI ask for IELTS Academic or OET. See how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

How to choose

  • Applying only for admission at universities that accept it: take the Duolingo English Test. It’s cheaper and faster.
  • Planning to work, move with family or apply for residence later in the UK, Canada, Australia or New Zealand: take IELTS (UKVI version for UK visas, General Training for Canada PR), so you only pay once.
  • Applying for a scholarship: check its own rules. Some, such as Australia Awards, name IELTS, TOEFL or PTE.

Tips for the Duolingo English Test

  • Use a quiet room, a laptop with a working camera and microphone, and a stable internet connection. A dropped connection can cancel your result.
  • Read the rules before you start: you can’t use headphones, notes or a second screen, and you must look at the screen.
  • Take the free practice test on the official site first, so the question types don’t surprise you.

Requirements change, so confirm on your university’s page and the official immigration website before you book.

title: Ireland's Critical Skills Employment Permit: salary rules, jobs and family in 2026
description: Ireland's Critical Skills permit lets skilled workers from Africa bring their family straight away and move to residence after two years. Here are the 2026 salary rules, fees and how to apply.

facts.label: Minimum salary
facts.value: €40,904 for jobs on the Critical Skills list (with a relevant degree), €68,911 for most other jobs

facts.label: Recent graduates
facts.value: €36,848 if you qualified in the last 12 months

facts.label: Fee
facts.value: €1,000, with 90% back if refused

facts.label: Family
facts.value: Can join you straight away, and your spouse can work

body:
Ireland is one of the best English-speaking countries for skilled workers right now. Its Critical Skills Employment Permit is aimed at jobs Ireland can’t fill locally, such as IT, engineering, nursing and medicine. It also lets your family come with you from the start.

Salary rules from 1 March 2026

You need a job offer that pays at least:

  • €40,904 a year for a job on Ireland’s Critical Skills Occupations List, where the job needs a relevant degree or higher, or
  • €36,848 a year for the same jobs if you got your qualification in the last 12 months, or
  • €68,911 a year for almost any other job, unless it’s on Ireland’s list of ineligible jobs.

Nurses and midwives need a qualification accepted by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI). See how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

If your job isn’t on the list and pays less than €68,911, look at Ireland’s General Employment Permit, which starts at €36,605. We compare both in moving abroad beyond Canada.

Jobs on the Critical Skills list

The list is based on Ireland’s skills shortages. It includes many:

  • ICT professionals, such as software developers, data and cloud roles,
  • professional engineers and technologists,
  • doctors, nurses and other health professionals.

Check the full, current list on the official page before you apply, as it’s reviewed regularly.

The job offer

  • The offer must be for at least 2 years.
  • You’re expected to stay with your first employer for at least 9 months, unless you’re made redundant or the job changes completely.
  • Your employer can’t make you pay back the permit fee.

Fees

The permit costs €1,000. If it’s refused, 90% is refunded. You’ll also pay for your visa (if you need one) and for your residence registration after you arrive.

Family

This is where the Critical Skills permit beats most work visas:

  • Your spouse or partner and children can apply to join you straight away.
  • Once they live in Ireland, your spouse or partner can work in any job, with a free Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit.

Path to residence

When your permit ends, usually after 2 years, you can apply to the Department of Justice for Stamp 4 permission. With Stamp 4, you can work for any employer without a permit. After 5 years (60 months) of permission, you can apply for long-term residence.

How to get started

  1. Check your job is on the Critical Skills list, or that your offer pays at least €68,911.
  2. Search for jobs with Irish employers that sponsor permits, and apply directly on their websites.
  3. Once you have an offer, you or your employer applies online through the Department’s employment permits system.
  4. After the permit is granted, apply for your visa if your nationality needs one.

Never pay a recruiter to “buy” an Irish job or permit. Real Irish employers don’t charge for jobs. Read how to spot fake job abroad offers before you send money to anyone.

title: Proof of funds for a student visa in 2026: UK, Canada and Germany
description: How much money you must show for a student visa to the UK, Canada or Germany in 2026, how long it must sit in your account, and how to avoid the mistakes that get visas refused.

facts.label: UK
facts.value: £1,529 a month in London or £1,171 elsewhere, for up to 9 months, plus first-year fees

facts.label: Canada
facts.value: CAD 23,448 for one person (from 1 September 2026), plus tuition and travel

facts.label: Germany
facts.value: €11,904 a year, usually in a blocked account

body:
Getting a university offer is only half the journey. To get a student visa, you must also prove you can pay for your studies and your living costs, and each country has its own amount and rules.

Here’s what the UK, Canada and Germany ask for in 2026, and how to prepare your bank statements so they don’t get your visa refused.

UK Student visa

For living costs, you must show:

  • £1,529 a month if you’ll study in London, or
  • £1,171 a month anywhere else in the UK,

for up to 9 months. That’s up to £13,761 for London and £10,539 elsewhere. You also need enough to pay your first year’s course fees, which are shown on your CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies), minus anything you’ve already paid.

The money must have been in your account for at least 28 days in a row, and the end of that 28-day period must be within 31 days of the day you apply. You need extra money for each family member you bring.

If your money is in naira, cedis, shillings or rand, keep a buffer above the minimum, because the amount is checked in pounds and exchange rates move.

Official: GOV.UK, money you need for a Student visa

Canada study permit

For study permit applications received on or after 1 September 2026, you must show CAD 23,448 for one person for a year of living costs, outside Quebec. Applications before that date needed CAD 22,895.

This amount doesn’t include tuition or travel: you must show your first year’s tuition and your travel costs on top. Bringing family raises the amount; IRCC publishes a table by family size. Quebec sets its own amounts.

IRCC accepts several kinds of proof, including:

  • bank statements for the past 6 months, showing where the money came from,
  • a guaranteed investment certificate (GIC) from a Canadian bank,
  • receipts for tuition and housing already paid,
  • a scholarship or student loan letter,
  • a letter from a sponsor, with their job, income and ID.

Official: IRCC, proof of financial support

Before you choose Canada, read what the study permit cap means for African students.

Germany student visa

Germany expects you to show €11,904 for a year of study, about €992 a month. Most students do this with a blocked account (Sperrkonto): you deposit the full amount before your visa appointment, and once you’re in Germany you can take out a fixed amount each month.

Other accepted proof includes:

  • a scholarship award letter from a recognised scholarship provider,
  • a formal guarantee from someone who lives permanently in Germany,
  • proof of your parents’ income and assets.

Embassies sometimes ask for a different amount, so confirm with the German embassy or consulate in your country before you pay into a blocked account.

Official: Study in Germany (DAAD), proof of financing

Mistakes that get visas refused

  • Money that appears just before you apply. A large deposit with no clear source looks borrowed. Keep the money in the account early, and be ready to show where it came from, such as salary, business income or the sale of property.
  • Statements that don’t meet the rules. Each country has rules on dates, names and stamps. Check them before you print.
  • Sponsors with no proof. If a parent or relative is paying, include their letter, ID, proof of relationship and their own bank statements.
  • Forgetting fees. The UK and Canada both expect tuition on top of living costs.
  • Paying an “agent” to provide funds. Fake or rented statements can get you banned from reapplying. See how to spot fake job and visa offers.

Scholarships change everything

A fully funded scholarship usually counts as proof of funds. See the awards open to Africans in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

Amounts change often, so always check the official page on the day you apply.

title: How to write a statement of purpose that wins scholarships
description: A clear, step-by-step way to write a statement of purpose or scholarship essay, with a structure that works, mistakes that sink applications, and a checklist before you submit.

facts.label: Length
facts.value: Usually 500 to 1,000 words, or exactly the limit the form gives

facts.label: Time to write
facts.value: Start 4 to 6 weeks before the deadline

facts.label: Golden rule
facts.value: Write a new one for every course and scholarship

body:
Your statement of purpose is often the only place a scholarship committee hears your voice. Grades and references show what you’ve done. The statement shows where you’re going, and why giving you the money makes sense.

Most applications from Africa are turned down for the same few reasons: the statement is generic, it tells a long life story, or it never says what the applicant will do after the course. This guide shows you how to avoid all three.

What the committee wants to know

Every good statement answers five questions:

  1. What do you want to study? Name the course, not just the field.
  2. Why this course and this university? Mention modules, research groups or teachers that match your plans.
  3. What have you done so far? Your degree, work, projects and results, with numbers where you can.
  4. What will you do after? A specific job, project or change you’ll make at home.
  5. Why you? What makes you more likely than other applicants to use this chance well.

If a paragraph doesn’t answer one of these, cut it.

A structure that works

Opening (one short paragraph). Start with the problem you want to solve, not your childhood. For example: “In my three years as a nurse in Kano, I saw mothers travel 60 km for a scan that could be done in their village.”

Your background (two paragraphs). What you studied, what you’ve done at work, and what you achieved. Use evidence: “I trained 14 health workers” beats “I am passionate about health”.

Why this course (one or two paragraphs). Link the course to your plan. Name two or three modules, a professor’s research or a practical part of the course, and say how each one helps.

Your plan after the course (one paragraph). Be specific about the role, the organisation or the project, and what will change because of it. Scholarships funded by governments and foundations especially want to see that you’ll use the skills at home.

Closing (two or three sentences). Bring it back to the problem from your opening, and say in one line why you’re ready.

Mistakes that sink applications

  • One statement for every application. Committees can tell. Change the course, university and plan for each one.
  • Starting with “Since I was a child”. It wastes your best lines. Start with the problem or your work.
  • Lists of qualities. “Hardworking, passionate and dedicated” says nothing. Show it with an example.
  • No plan after the course. This is the most common reason strong candidates lose.
  • Copying templates or letting AI write it. Reviewers read thousands of statements, and copied or machine-written text sounds the same. Use tools to check grammar, but the story and the plan must be yours.
  • Ignoring the word limit. Going over can get you rejected before anyone reads it.

Scholarship essays are different

Some scholarships ask several short questions instead of one statement, for example about leadership, networking or your career plan. Answer each question directly, and use a different example in each answer. The same five questions above still apply, just spread across the answers.

Before you submit: a checklist

  • It names the exact course and university.
  • Every paragraph answers one of the five questions.
  • There’s at least one number or result in your background section.
  • Your plan after the course is specific enough that someone could check it in five years.
  • Someone who knows your field has read it, and someone outside your field understood it.
  • It’s within the word limit, with no spelling mistakes.

Where to use it

Your statement is ready to adapt for the big awards in our 2027 scholarship calendar, including Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus and DAAD EPOS. Check each scholarship’s own instructions for length and questions, as they differ.

title: Germany Is Looking for Skilled Workers. Could You Qualify?
description: Germany is hiring skilled workers from outside Europe. Here are the four main routes, the 2026 salary for the EU Blue Card, and the first steps for Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians and South Africans.

facts.label: Main routes
facts.value: EU Blue Card, skilled worker visa, Opportunity Card

facts.label: Blue Card salary
facts.value: €50,700 a year in 2026, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs

facts.label: Key step
facts.value: Get your degree or training recognised in Germany

facts.label: Language
facts.value: German helps most; some IT and research jobs use English

body:
Germany has more jobs than workers in many fields, and it has changed its immigration rules to bring in people from outside Europe. Nurses, engineers, IT specialists, electricians and other trained workers from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia can all apply.

You don’t need to know someone in Germany, and you don’t pay an agent. But you do need the right qualification, and for most routes, a job offer first.

The four main routes

1. EU Blue Card. For people with a university degree and a job offer that pays enough. In 2026 the salary is €50,700 a year, or €45,934.20 for shortage jobs such as IT, engineering, medicine and nursing, and for graduates in their first three years after their degree. IT specialists with 3 years’ experience can qualify without a degree. The Blue Card is the fastest way to permanent residence.

2. Skilled worker visa. For people with a recognised degree or at least two years of vocational training (for example, electricians, plumbers, mechanics or nurses) and a job offer in their field. There’s no fixed salary for most applicants under 45.

3. Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte). Lets you move to Germany for up to a year without a job offer to look for one, and work part-time while you search. It uses a points system. See our full guide to the Opportunity Card.

4. Recognition partnership. If your qualification is only partly recognised, an employer can hire you while you complete the missing training in Germany.

Salary figures for 2026 were published by the German government in late 2025. When we checked, the Make it in Germany page still showed the 2025 amounts (€48,300 and €43,759.80), so confirm the current figure there before you apply.

Could you qualify? A quick check

You have a good chance if you can say yes to most of these:

  • I have a university degree, or at least two years of formal vocational training.
  • I have worked in my field for at least two years.
  • I’m learning German, or I already speak it at A2 or higher.
  • My job is one Germany is short of: nursing and care, IT, engineering, skilled trades, or teaching.

If you’re missing the job offer, the Opportunity Card is built for you. If you’re missing the qualification, a German vocational training place (Ausbildung) is another way in.

Get your qualification recognised first

This is the step most people skip, and it’s the reason many visa applications fail. The German Foreign Office says that without recognition of your foreign degree or certificate, your visa application can’t be processed.

  • Degrees: check whether your university and degree are listed in the anabin database. For many non-regulated jobs, that’s enough.
  • Regulated jobs (nursing, medicine, teaching and some others): you need permission to practise from the German authority for that job.
  • Vocational training: apply for recognition through the Recognition in Germany portal, which shows which office handles your job.

How to apply

  1. Check your route on Make it in Germany, the German government’s official site for skilled workers.
  2. Start recognition of your qualification.
  3. Learn German. Even A2 makes job hunting much easier.
  4. Apply for jobs on the Federal Employment Agency’s job board and on Make it in Germany.
  5. Once you have an offer, book a national visa appointment at the German embassy in your country and bring the employer’s “Declaration regarding a contract of employment”.

Avoid the scams

Real German employers don’t charge you for a job or a visa. Be careful with anyone who promises a guaranteed job, asks for money for a “work permit”, or wants payment before an interview. Read how to spot a fake job abroad offer before you pay anyone.

Nurses should also read how nurses from Africa can work in the UK or Ireland to compare their options.

title: Thinking of Moving Abroad? Look Beyond Canada
description: Canada is cutting the number of newcomers it lets in, but it isn't the only option. Here's how Germany, the UK, Ireland and Australia compare for skilled workers from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa.

facts.label: Germany
facts.value: EU Blue Card from €50,700 (2026), or a 1-year job-search visa

facts.label: UK
facts.value: Skilled Worker visa from £41,700, degree-level jobs, B2 English

facts.label: Ireland
facts.value: Critical Skills permit from €40,904, General permit from €36,605

facts.label: Australia
facts.value: Skills in Demand visa from AUD 79,499 (from 1 July 2026)

body:
For years, Canada was the first choice for Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians and South Africans planning to move abroad. That has changed. Canada is issuing fewer study permits and cutting the number of temporary residents, so competition for every place is tougher.

Canada is still worth considering, but it shouldn’t be your only plan. Several other countries are actively hiring skilled workers from Africa, and some are easier to reach.

Germany: the most open door right now

Germany is short of workers in nursing, IT, engineering and skilled trades, and it has made its rules simpler.

  • EU Blue Card: for graduates with a job offer paying at least €50,700 a year in 2026, or €45,934.20 in shortage jobs.
  • Skilled worker visa: for people with a recognised degree or vocational training and a job offer.
  • Opportunity Card: move for up to a year without a job offer to look for work.

The catch is language: most jobs need some German. Read our guide to whether you could qualify for Germany.

United Kingdom: harder than before, still open

The UK Skilled Worker visa now needs a degree-level job, a salary of at least £41,700 (or the job’s going rate) and B2 English. The care worker route has closed to people applying from abroad, but nurses can still go through the Health and Care Worker visa.

See the new UK Skilled Worker rules and what replaced the UK care visa.

Ireland: English-speaking and hiring

Ireland uses employment permits. From 1 March 2026:

  • the Critical Skills Employment Permit needs a salary of at least €40,904, for jobs on Ireland’s critical skills list such as ICT, engineering, nursing and medicine, and
  • the General Employment Permit needs at least €36,605, for most other jobs not on the ineligible list.

Critical Skills holders can bring family and move towards long-term residence. Nurses can register with the NMBI: see how nurses can work in the UK or Ireland.

Australia: high pay, high bar

Australia’s Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) needs an employer sponsor. From 1 July 2026, the Core Skills stream needs a salary of at least AUD 79,499. Australia also runs points-tested permanent visas for people with skills on its occupation lists, but they need strong English and a skills assessment.

For a master’s, Australia Awards Africa funds study for mid-career professionals: see our 2027 scholarship calendar.

How they compare

CountryJob offer first?English only?Best for
GermanyNot with the Opportunity CardUsually no, German helpsNurses, engineers, IT, trades
UKYesYesDegree-level jobs, nurses
IrelandYesYesIT, engineering, health
AustraliaYes, for the 482YesExperienced professionals

Before you go anywhere

  • Use only the official government sites to check the rules. Each country’s visa site is free to read.
  • Never pay for a job offer. Read how to spot a fake job abroad offer.
  • Start your English test or German classes now. They take the longest.

Salary thresholds and rules change every year, so check the official page for each country before you apply.

title: Planning to Study Abroad in 2027? Explore Scholarship Opportunities
description: If you want to start a degree abroad in 2027, the scholarship deadlines are now. Here's a month-by-month plan and the big fully funded awards open to Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians and South Africans.

facts.label: Best time to start
facts.value: Now: most 2027 deadlines fall between November 2026 and March 2027

facts.label: Open now
facts.value: Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus, DAAD EPOS, Mastercard Foundation partners

facts.label: Opening soon
facts.value: Türkiye Bursları (10 Jan), Australia Awards Africa (1 Feb 2027)

body:
If you want to start a master’s, PhD or undergraduate degree abroad in September 2027, now is the time to apply for funding. Most fully funded scholarships close 8 to 12 months before the course starts, and if you miss a window, you wait a full year.

The good news: many of the biggest scholarships are open to students from Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia, and they cover tuition, living costs and flights.

Scholarships open now

  • Gates Cambridge: PhD and most one-year master’s courses at the University of Cambridge. Deadlines are 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the course.
  • Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters: study in two or more European countries, with about €1,400 a month. Each course sets its own deadline, usually between October and January.
  • DAAD EPOS: master’s and PhD courses in Germany for people with at least two years’ work experience. Each course sets its deadline.
  • Mastercard Foundation Scholars: undergraduate and master’s study at partner universities in Africa and abroad.

Opening soon

  • Türkiye Bursları: all levels in Türkiye. The window usually runs from 10 January to 20 February.
  • Australia Awards Africa: master’s in Australia for professionals with at least 5 years’ work experience. The next round opens on 1 February 2027.

See all twelve, with what each covers, in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

Your plan, month by month

WhenWhat to do
Now (October to November)Pick 3 to 5 scholarships and courses. Ask two referees for letters.
November to DecemberTake IELTS or another English test if you need it. Write your statement of purpose.
December to JanuarySubmit applications for Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus and DAAD courses.
January to MarchApply for Türkiye Bursları and Australia Awards. Prepare for interviews.
April to JuneResults arrive. Accept an offer and start your visa application.

If you need an English test, see what IELTS costs in Nigeria and book early, because test dates fill up before big deadlines.

What makes an application stand out

  • A clear plan. Committees want to know what you’ll study, why that course, and what you’ll do with it at home.
  • Proof you lead. Community projects, work achievements or starting something count as much as grades.
  • Strong references. Pick people who know your work well, and give them at least a month.
  • Applying to several. Even strong candidates are turned down by most scholarships, so apply to more than one.

Thinking about Canada?

Canada is giving out fewer study permits than before. Read what the Canada study permit cap means for African students before you decide.

Always confirm deadlines on each scholarship’s official page before you apply, as programmes can change them.

title: Canada study permit cap 2026: what it means for African students
description: Canada is issuing fewer study permits in 2026 and plans 150,000 new student arrivals a year in 2027 and 2028. Master's and PhD students at public institutions no longer need a PAL.

facts.label: 2026 cap
facts.value: 408,000 study permits, including 155,000 new arrivals

facts.label: 2027 and 2028
facts.value: 150,000 new student arrivals planned each year

facts.label: PAL
facts.value: Not needed for master's and PhD at public institutions from 1 January 2026

body:
Canada is still one of the most popular study destinations for Nigerians, Ghanaians and Kenyans, but there are fewer places than before. Here’s what the cap means and who it affects least.

How many study permits Canada is issuing

YearStudy permits
2025437,000
2026408,000, including 155,000 for new arrivals
2027150,000 new student arrivals planned
2028150,000 new student arrivals planned

Sources: 2026 allocations under the student cap, Immigration levels plan 2026–2028.

Good news for master’s and PhD students

Most applicants need a provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL), which shows the province has a place for you under the cap.

From 1 January 2026, master’s and PhD students at public institutions don’t need a PAL. If you’re planning a postgraduate degree at a public university, the cap affects you much less than it affects college and undergraduate applicants.

What this means if you’re applying

  1. Apply early. With fewer places, colleges and provinces may run out of PALs before the end of the intake.
  2. Choose a designated learning institution (DLI). Only schools on the DLI list can accept international students. IRCC warns about fake schools and offers, so check the DLI list and IRCC’s fraud and scams page before you pay a deposit.
  3. Consider a postgraduate degree. Master’s and PhD programmes at public universities skip the PAL.

Thinking about staying after you study?

Canada is also changing Express Entry. From 3 November 2026, it adds points for high-wage occupations and drops the need for an LMIA for qualifying job offers. IRCC news release.

Want funding? See our 2027 scholarship calendar.

title: DAAD EPOS scholarship: a funded master's or PhD in Germany for professionals
description: DAAD's EPOS programme pays €934 a month for a development-related master's in Germany (€1,300 for a PhD). Here's who qualifies and how the course-by-course deadlines work.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Master's or PhD, 12 to 42 months

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Professionals from developing countries with 2+ years' work experience

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: €934 a month (master's) or €1,300 (PhD), insurance and travel

facts.label: Deadline
facts.value: Set by each course, usually June to December before the start

body:
EPOS stands for Development-Related Postgraduate Courses. It’s a DAAD (German Academic Exchange Service) programme that funds professionals from developing countries to take selected master’s and PhD courses in Germany, in fields such as public health, engineering, agriculture, economics and environmental management.

Unlike many scholarships, you don’t apply to DAAD directly. You apply to the course, and the course selects its scholarship holders.

What the scholarship pays

  • €934 a month for master’s students, or €1,300 a month for PhD students.
  • Health, accident and personal liability insurance.
  • A travel allowance.
  • In some cases, a rent subsidy and a family allowance.

Courses last between 12 and 42 months, and many are taught in English.

Who can apply

You must be a national of a country on the OECD’s list of aid recipients. That list includes Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa, along with most African countries. You also need:

  • a bachelor’s degree, usually no more than 6 years old when you apply, and
  • at least 2 years of relevant work experience after that degree.

Each course adds its own requirements, such as a minimum grade or an English test score.

How to apply

  1. Look at the EPOS course list in the DAAD scholarship database and pick up to 3 courses.
  2. Rank them in order of preference.
  3. Apply through each course’s own process, by its own deadline.

When to apply

DAAD’s list of deadlines for courses starting in 2027/28 says “see website of the course” for every course, because each course sets its own. In the last round, most deadlines fell between June and December of the year before the course started. Check your courses now, because some may close before the end of 2026.

Tips

  • Your motivation letter should link your work experience to the course and say how you’ll use the degree back home.
  • Get a letter from your employer that confirms your work experience, with dates.
  • Apply to courses that genuinely match your field: EPOS courses look for relevant experience, not just good grades.

Find more funded courses in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

title: Erasmus Mundus scholarship: €1,400 a month to study a master's in Europe
description: How Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarships work for Africans: what they pay, how to apply to each course, and when applications open.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Master's (12 to 24 months)

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Students from any country

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: No tuition fees, plus €1,400 a month for the whole course

facts.label: Applications
facts.value: Usually October to January, set by each course

body:
Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are master’s programmes run by groups of European universities. You often study in two or three countries during one degree, and the best applicants get a scholarship that covers everything.

There isn’t one central application. Each course runs its own admissions and picks its own scholarship holders, so you can apply to more than one.

What the scholarship pays

  • No tuition or application fees for scholarship holders.
  • €1,400 a month for the full length of the programme, which runs for 12 to 24 months.

The monthly allowance is meant to cover your travel, visa and living costs, so plan your budget around it.

Who can apply

Students from any country can apply, including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia. To keep courses international, no more than 10% of a course’s scholarships can go to students of one nationality, and some places are reserved for applicants from particular regions.

You’ll need a bachelor’s degree (or to finish it before the course starts) and the course’s English requirement, usually shown as an IELTS or TOEFL score.

How to apply

  1. Search the Erasmus Mundus catalogue for courses in your field.
  2. Open each course’s own website and read its entry requirements and deadline.
  3. Apply on that course’s site and tick the scholarship option. Most courses ask for a CV, a motivation letter, transcripts, references and an English test result.

When to apply

Applications usually open between October and January for courses starting the following September. Each course sets its own closing date, and popular courses often close in December or January, so start now.

Tips

  • Apply to two or three courses that genuinely match your degree. The motivation letter should explain why that exact course fits your plans.
  • Read the selection criteria on each course page. Many score grades, relevant experience and the letter separately.
  • Keep your documents ready as PDFs, because each course has its own portal.

More awards are in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

title: Fully funded scholarships for Africans: the 2027 calendar
description: 12 big scholarships Nigerians, Kenyans, Ghanaians, South Africans, Zimbabweans and Zambians can apply for, with what each covers and when it opens or closes.

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: 12 scholarships for master's, PhD and undergraduate study

facts.label: Open now
facts.value: Gates Cambridge, Erasmus Mundus courses, DAAD EPOS courses, Mastercard Foundation partners

body:
Most fully funded scholarships open once a year and close months before the course starts. If you miss a window, you wait a full year. This calendar shows where each major scholarship stands right now, so you know which to apply for today and which to prepare for.

Every entry links to the official page. Dates were checked on 22 October 2026, but programmes do change them, so confirm on the official site before you start.

Open now

ScholarshipLevelWhereDeadline
Gates CambridgePhD, most one-year master’sUK8 Dec 2026 or 6 Jan 2027, depending on the course
Erasmus Mundus Joint MastersMaster’sEuropeSet by each course, usually October to January
DAAD EPOSMaster’s, PhDGermanySet by each course
Mastercard Foundation ScholarsUndergraduate, master’sAfrica, UK, USA, CanadaSet by each partner university

Opening soon

  • Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships): undergraduate, master’s and PhD in Türkiye for citizens of every country. The application window usually runs from 10 January to 20 February. It covers tuition, accommodation, health insurance, a one-year Turkish course, flights and a monthly stipend. Official calendar.
  • Australia Awards Africa: master’s in Australia for mid-career professionals with at least 5 years’ work experience. The next round opens on 1 February 2027. Official site.
  • Stipendium Hungaricum: bachelor’s, master’s and PhD in Hungary. The last deadline was 15 January 2026, and in Nigeria applications go through the Federal Scholarship Board. The 2027/28 call hadn’t been published when we checked. Hungarian embassy, Abuja.

Closed for 2027 (prepare for the next round)

  • Chevening (UK): one-year master’s for people with at least 2 years’ work experience. The 2027/28 round opened in August 2026 and is now closed. Expect the next one around August 2027. Chevening timeline.
  • Commonwealth Master’s Scholarships (UK): tuition, flights and a monthly stipend of £1,712 (£2,000 in London). The 2027/28 round closed on 20 October 2026. You apply through your country’s nominating agency. CSC master’s page.
  • Rhodes Scholarship (Oxford): separate places for West Africa (including Nigeria and Ghana), Kenya, Southern Africa (including South Africa), Zambia and Zimbabwe. The 2027 deadlines were in August 2026. Rhodes constituencies.
  • Japan MEXT (embassy recommendation): master’s, PhD and undergraduate study in Japan. The 2027 rounds closed in May and June 2026. Embassies usually open the next round in April. Study in Japan.
  • Fulbright Foreign Student Program (USA): run by each US embassy. Kenya’s 2027/28 round closed on 20 April 2026. Nigerians should note that the US has partly suspended student and exchange visas (F, M and J) for Nigerian citizens since 1 January 2026. US Embassy Nigeria update.

How to use this calendar

  1. Pick 3 or 4 scholarships that match your level and work experience.
  2. Note when each one opens, and start your documents two months before: transcripts, references and your personal statement.
  3. Most master’s scholarships expect an English test. See our guide to the IELTS fee in Nigeria if you need one.

Check the deadlines page for every open application, closing soonest first.

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship 2027: who can apply and the deadlines
description: Gates Cambridge pays full fees, a £23,152 living allowance and flights for a PhD or master's at Cambridge. Applications for 2027 are open now.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: PhD, MLitt and most one-year postgraduate courses

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Citizens of any country outside the UK

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: Full fees, £23,152 a year to live on, flights, visa and the UK health surcharge

body:
The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is one of the most generous awards in the world. It pays for a full postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge, and it’s open to applicants from every country outside the UK, including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia.

Applications for courses starting in 2027 opened on 11 September 2026.

What the scholarship pays

  • The full cost of your Cambridge course fees.
  • A living allowance of £23,152 a year (the 2026-27 rate).
  • One economy return flight at the start and end of your course.
  • The cost of your student visa and the UK immigration health surcharge.
  • Extra money for children may be available, at the Trust’s discretion.

Who can apply

You can apply if you’re a citizen of any country except the UK and you’re applying for a full-time PhD, MLitt or most one-year postgraduate courses at Cambridge. Some courses aren’t covered, including the MBA, the MASt and undergraduate degrees. Check eligibility.

The Trust looks for four things: outstanding intellectual ability, leadership potential, a commitment to improving the lives of others, and a good fit between you and your chosen course.

How to apply

There’s no separate scholarship form. You apply for your Cambridge course through the university’s graduate application portal and tick the box to be considered for Gates Cambridge funding. Your application, references and a short Gates statement are reviewed together.

Deadlines for 2027

DeadlineWho it’s for
8 December 2026Applicants whose course has the December funding deadline
6 January 2027Applicants whose course has the January funding deadline

The deadline that applies to you depends on your course, and it’s shown on the course page on the Cambridge website. Results are due by 8 March 2027.

Tips

  1. Start with the course, not the scholarship. Your department’s view of you matters a lot.
  2. Ask your referees early, because both references must arrive before your course’s deadline.
  3. Use the Gates statement to show what you have already done for others, not just what you plan to do.

See the full scholarship calendar for more awards open now.

title: Germany Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte): a one-year visa to look for work
description: Germany's Opportunity Card lets skilled people move to Germany for up to a year to find a job, with part-time work allowed. Here's who qualifies and how much money you need.

facts.label: Valid for
facts.value: Up to 1 year

facts.label: Work allowed
facts.value: Part-time, up to 20 hours a week

facts.label: Money needed
facts.value: €1,091 a month in a blocked account (2026)

body:
Most work visas need a job offer first. Germany’s Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) works the other way round: it lets you move to Germany for up to a year to look for a job, and work part-time while you search.

It’s open to people from any country outside the EU, including Nigerians, Ghanaians, Kenyans, South Africans, Zimbabweans and Zambians.

Who qualifies

There are two ways in.

1. Your qualification is fully recognised in Germany. If a German authority has already recognised your degree or vocational qualification as equal to a German one, you qualify without points.

2. You score at least 6 points. For this route you need:

  • a university degree, or at least 2 years of vocational training, that is recognised in your home country,
  • German at A1 level or English at B2 level, and
  • at least 6 points.
What you havePoints
Qualification partly recognised in Germany4
Qualification in a shortage occupation1
Work experience: 2+ years in the last 52
Work experience: 5+ years in the last 73
German A2 / B1 / B2 or higher1 / 2 / 3
English C1 or higher (or native speaker)1
Age under 352
Age 35 to 401
6+ months’ legal stay in Germany in the last 5 years (not as a tourist)1
Spouse or partner who also qualifies for the card1

For example, a 30-year-old nurse with 5 years’ experience and German B1 scores 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 points.

Source: Make it in Germany.

How much money you need

You must show you can support yourself while you search. The usual way is a blocked account holding €1,091 for each month of your stay in 2026. For a full year, that’s €13,092.

The other option is a declaration of commitment, where someone in Germany formally agrees to cover your costs.

What you can do with it

  • Stay in Germany for up to 1 year.
  • Work part-time, up to 20 hours a week.
  • Do trial work for up to 2 weeks per employer.
  • Switch to a residence permit for skilled work in Germany once you find a qualifying job, without going home first.

How to apply

  1. Check your points or get your qualification recognised.
  2. Open a blocked account and arrange health insurance.
  3. Book a national visa appointment at the German embassy or consulate for your country.
  4. Pay the €75 visa fee and submit your documents.

The German Embassy in Accra lists the fee and documents on its visa information page. Check the page for your own country before your appointment, as document lists can differ.

Tips

  • Learning German is the biggest advantage you can give yourself. It earns points for the card, and most jobs in Germany need it.
  • Start applying for jobs before you travel, so you use your year well.
  • Nurses and care professionals should look at Germany’s recognition process for health jobs, which is separate from the Opportunity Card.

Looking at other countries? See routes open to carers and nurses.

title: IELTS fee in Nigeria (2026): British Council and IDP prices compared
description: IELTS Academic and General Training cost ₦299,000 in Nigeria in 2026, and IELTS for UKVI costs ₦301,200 to ₦315,500. Here are the current prices and a ₦25,000 British Council discount.

facts.label: IELTS for UKVI
facts.value: ₦301,200 (British Council) or ₦315,500 (IDP)

facts.label: Discount
facts.value: ₦25,000 off at British Council until 31 December 2026

body:
IELTS is run in Nigeria by two organisations, the British Council and IDP. Both sell the same tests with the same results, but their prices for some tests differ.

These are the prices shown on their official pages in October 2026.

IELTS fees in Nigeria

TestBritish CouncilIDP
IELTS Academic or General Training₦299,000₦299,000 (computer-delivered)
IELTS for UKVI₦301,200₦315,500
IELTS Life Skills₦285,200₦298,500

Sources: British Council IELTS Academic, British Council IELTS for UKVI, IDP Nigeria test dates.

You may still see older pages showing ₦266,000 or ₦75,000. Those figures are out of date, so budget with the prices above.

The ₦25,000 British Council discount

The British Council is offering ₦25,000 off when you book with the code NGBCIELTS26. It runs from 14 July to 31 December 2026 and is limited to the first 50 bookings each week, so book early in the week. Details on the British Council site.

Which IELTS test do you need?

  • IELTS Academic: for university admission abroad, and for nurses registering in the UK or Ireland.
  • IELTS General Training: for work and migration to Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
  • IELTS for UKVI: for UK visas, such as the Skilled Worker or Health and Care Worker visa.
  • IELTS Life Skills: for some UK family and settlement visas, where only speaking and listening are tested.

If you’re applying for a UK visa, check that you book the UKVI version. A normal IELTS Academic result can’t be used for most UK visa applications.

What score you need

PurposeScore
UK Skilled Worker or Health and Care Worker visaIELTS for UKVI 5.5 in each skill (B2)
Nursing in the UK or IrelandIELTS Academic 7.0 in listening, reading and speaking, 6.5 in writing
University admissionSet by each university, often 6.0 to 7.0 overall

Read more about the UK Skilled Worker English rules and nurse registration in the UK and Ireland.

Other UK-approved tests

The UK also accepts LanguageCert, Pearson PTE (UKVI and Home), PSI Skills for English and Trinity tests for visas. GOV.UK list of approved tests. Compare their fees and test dates near you before you book.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program: how to apply and which universities are open
description: Mastercard Foundation scholarships pay tuition, accommodation, books and flights for young Africans. You apply to a partner university, and each one has its own deadline.

facts.label: Level
facts.value: Secondary, undergraduate and master's

facts.label: Who can apply
facts.value: Young Africans (29 or under for undergraduate, 35 or under for master's)

facts.label: Covers
facts.value: Tuition, accommodation, books, mentoring and a return flight if needed

body:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is one of the largest scholarship programmes for Africans. It funds young people with strong grades and limited money to study at partner universities in Africa and abroad, and it supports them with mentoring and leadership training along the way.

Priority goes to young women, people with disabilities and young people who have been displaced.

What the scholarship pays

  • Tuition.
  • Accommodation.
  • Books and study materials.
  • Mentoring and leadership support.
  • A return flight, if your university is outside your home country.

Who can apply

  • Young Africans from any African country, including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia.
  • For undergraduate study you should be 29 or younger, and for a master’s 35 or younger.
  • You need strong academic results and evidence of financial need.

There are no PhD places.

How to apply

There is no single Mastercard Foundation application. You apply to a partner university, and the university runs the selection. Each partner sets its own requirements and deadline.

When we checked the Foundation’s partner pages, these were shown as open:

UniversityCountryLevel
KNUSTGhanaUndergraduate
University of EdinburghUKPostgraduate
University of CambridgeUKPostgraduate
Arizona State UniversityUSAPostgraduate

The University of Pretoria and USIU-Africa were shown as closed. Statuses change through the year, so check the Foundation’s list of where to apply and the university’s own page.

Tips

  1. Read each university’s page carefully. Some partners only accept certain fields or certain countries.
  2. Show both your grades and your financial need. You’ll usually need documents for both.
  3. Write about how you plan to give back to your community. It’s central to how the programme selects scholars.

See what else is open in our 2027 scholarship calendar.

title: How nurses from Africa can work in the UK or Ireland: NMC and NMBI registration
description: Nurses can still move to the UK and Ireland from abroad. Here are the registration steps, the IELTS and OET scores you need, and the visa each country uses.

facts.label: UK steps
facts.value: NMC eligibility check, CBT, OSCE, then registration

facts.label: English
facts.value: IELTS Academic 7.0 (6.5 writing) or OET B, B, C+ writing, B

facts.label: UK visa
facts.value: Health and Care Worker visa, from £25,000 or NHS pay

facts.label: Ireland permit
facts.value: Critical Skills Employment Permit, from €40,904

body:
Nurses remain one of the strongest routes abroad for Africans. The UK closed its care worker visa to overseas applicants in 2025, but registered nurses can still apply from abroad to both the UK and Ireland.

In both countries you need to register with the nursing regulator before you can work as a nurse.

UK: registering with the NMC

The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) registers nurses trained outside the UK in four steps:

  1. Eligibility and qualification check. You apply online and the NMC checks your training and nursing registration at home.
  2. Computer-based test (CBT). A multiple-choice test of nursing knowledge, which you can take in your own country.
  3. OSCE. A practical clinical exam, taken in the UK.
  4. Registration. Once you pass, you join the register and can work as a nurse.

NMC: registering if you trained outside the UK.

English scores you need

TestScore for the NMC and NMBI
IELTS Academic7.0 in listening, reading and speaking, and 6.5 in writing (Ireland also needs 7.0 overall)
OETB in listening, reading and speaking, and C+ in writing

Ireland’s NMBI does not accept IELTS Online, OET@Home, the IELTS One Skill Retake, or results combined from more than one sitting, and results must be less than 2 years old. Book a test centre.

Sources: NMC accepted English tests, NMBI English requirements.

UK visa: Health and Care Worker

Nurses usually come on the Health and Care Worker visa. The job must pay at least £25,000, or the going rate or NHS pay scale for the role. Health and Care Worker visa holders don’t pay the immigration health surcharge. GOV.UK.

Ireland: registering with the NMBI

The Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI) assesses nurses trained outside the EU. After the assessment, you may be asked to complete compensation measures, such as a supervised adaptation period in an Irish hospital, before full registration.

Ireland visa: Critical Skills Employment Permit

Registered nurses (code 2231), midwives (2232) and doctors (2211) are on Ireland’s Critical Skills list. For these jobs:

  • the minimum salary is €40,904 for people with a relevant degree,
  • you need a job offer of at least 2 years, and
  • the permit fee is €1,000.

Ireland raised its permit salary thresholds on 1 March 2026 and plans to raise them each year until 2030. Department of Enterprise.

Also worth a look: Canada

Canada runs Express Entry draws for healthcare workers, including registered nurses, licensed practical nurses and nurse aides. You need at least 12 months of work in one listed job within the last 3 years. IRCC category-based selection.

Tips

  • Start the English test early. It’s the step most applicants repeat.
  • Keep your nursing licence at home active, as both regulators check it.
  • You don’t need an agent to register. The NMC and NMBI applications are online, and you pay the regulator directly.

title: How to spot a fake job abroad or visa offer before you pay
description: Fake visa sponsorship and job abroad offers cost Africans millions every year. Here's how to check an employer, a recruiter or a school in a few minutes.

facts.label: UK employers
facts.value: Check the register of licensed sponsors

facts.label: Canada
facts.value: Paid representatives must be licensed

facts.label: Rule of thumb
facts.value: Never pay for a job offer or a sponsorship certificate

body:
Every week, people lose money to “visa sponsorship” offers that don’t exist. The good news is that most fake offers can be spotted in a few minutes, using free official tools.

1. Check the employer is allowed to sponsor

UK: every employer that can sponsor a work visa is listed on the government’s register of licensed sponsors. If the company isn’t on it, it can’t give you a Skilled Worker or Health and Care Worker visa.

UK sponsors must also pay their own Immigration Skills Charge. GOV.UK warns that a sponsor’s licence may be revoked if it asks the worker to pay it or any costs linked to the application.

Canada: anyone you pay for immigration advice must be licensed. IRCC explains how to check on its fraud and scams page.

2. Warning signs

  • You’re asked to pay for the job offer, the certificate of sponsorship or a “work permit slot”.
  • The offer arrived without an interview, or after a short WhatsApp chat.
  • The salary is far above what the job normally pays.
  • The email comes from a free address (such as Gmail) rather than the company’s domain.
  • You’re pushed to pay quickly “before the slot is gone”.
  • The route doesn’t exist any more. For example, the UK care worker visa closed to overseas applicants in July 2025.

3. Check the school, if you’re studying

For Canada, your school must be a designated learning institution (DLI). For the UK, it must be a licensed student sponsor. Check before you pay a deposit.

4. Pay official fees to official places only

Visa fees are paid to the government, usually online through its official site or visa centre. Test fees are paid to the British Council, IDP or the test provider. If someone asks you to pay these through a personal bank account, stop.

5. Use the official pages

Each guide on AbroadPath links to the official page for that scholarship or visa. Use those links to check any offer you’re sent.

Start with our guides to the UK Skilled Worker visa, the Germany Opportunity Card and nursing in the UK and Ireland.

title: UK care worker visa is closed to new overseas applicants: where carers and nurses can go now
description: Since 22 July 2025 the UK no longer gives care worker visas to people applying from abroad. Here's what changed, who can still go, and the routes open to Africans in 2026.

facts.label: What changed
facts.value: Care worker and senior care worker visas closed to applicants abroad on 22 July 2025

facts.label: Still open
facts.value: Doctors, nurses, midwives and other health professionals

facts.label: Other options
facts.value: Ireland, Canada and Germany

body:
For years, “UK care jobs with visa sponsorship” was the most searched route abroad for Nigerians, Zimbabweans, Ghanaians and Kenyans. That door has now closed for anyone applying from outside the UK.

On 22 July 2025, the UK stopped giving Health and Care Worker visas to new overseas applicants for care worker (occupation code 6135) and senior care worker (6136) jobs. Any “care job with visa sponsorship” advertised to people abroad after that date can’t lead to a UK visa through this route.

Who is affected

  • People abroad: can no longer get a UK visa as a care worker or senior care worker.
  • Care workers already in the UK: can still switch or extend in the UK until 22 July 2028. The government says this is “kept under review”.

The numbers show the change. Health and Care main-applicant grants fell by 65% in the year to June 2026.

Who can still get a UK health visa from abroad

The Health and Care Worker visa is still open to qualified health professionals, including:

  • doctors,
  • nurses,
  • midwives, and
  • other registered health professionals.

The job must pay at least £25,000 or the going rate for the role (or the NHS pay scale for listed jobs), and Health and Care Worker visa holders don’t pay the immigration health surcharge. See GOV.UK.

If you’re a nurse, read our guide on registering as a nurse in the UK or Ireland.

Other routes open to Africans in 2026

Ireland: Critical Skills Employment Permit. Registered nurses, midwives and doctors are on Ireland’s Critical Skills list. The minimum salary is €40,904 for listed jobs with a relevant degree, and you need a job offer of at least 2 years. Department of Enterprise.

Canada: Express Entry healthcare draws. Canada runs category draws for healthcare and social services, including registered nurses, licensed practical nurses and nurse aides. You need at least 12 months of work in one listed job within the last 3 years. IRCC category-based selection.

Germany: Opportunity Card. A one-year job-search visa for skilled people with a recognised degree or vocational training. See our Opportunity Card guide.

Protect yourself

Because the care route has closed, be very careful with anyone selling “UK care visa sponsorship” to people abroad. Real UK employers don’t charge for a certificate of sponsorship. Check any offer against the official GOV.UK pages linked above before you pay anyone.

title: UK Skilled Worker visa in 2026: the new salary, skill and English rules
description: The UK Skilled Worker visa now needs a degree-level job, a salary of at least £41,700 and B2 English. Here's what changed and who still qualifies from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

facts.label: Minimum salary
facts.value: £41,700, or the job's going rate if higher

facts.label: Skill level
facts.value: Degree level (RQF 6) for most jobs since 22 July 2025

facts.label: English
facts.value: B2 since 8 January 2026 (IELTS for UKVI 5.5 in each skill)

facts.label: Graduate visa
facts.value: 18 months for applications from 1 January 2027

body:
The UK Skilled Worker visa is still open to people from every African country, but it’s much harder to qualify than it was two years ago. Three rules changed: the type of job, the salary, and the English level.

If you were planning to go as a care worker, read our guide on what replaced the UK care visa first, because that route has closed to people applying from abroad.

The job must be degree level

Since 22 July 2025, the job must be at RQF level 6, which is roughly degree level. Medium-skilled jobs only qualify if they are on one of two lists:

  • the Immigration Salary List, or
  • the Temporary Shortage List.

The Temporary Shortage List is time-limited to the end of 2026 unless the Migration Advisory Committee recommends keeping it. Workers who come through a job on that list can’t bring dependants.

The salary must be at least £41,700

The general minimum rose from £38,700 to £41,700 on 22 July 2025. If the going rate for your job is higher, you must be paid the going rate.

A lower minimum, from £33,400, applies in some cases, for example to some new entrants. GOV.UK lists the cases.

Doctors, nurses and other health professionals usually apply through the Health and Care Worker visa instead, which has a lower £25,000 floor or the NHS pay scale.

English is now B2

From 8 January 2026, Skilled Worker and Health and Care Worker applicants must prove English at B2 level, up from B1. Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia are not exempt, even though English is an official language.

With IELTS for UKVI, B2 means 5.5 in each of the four skills. See IELTS fees in Nigeria for what the test costs.

Other changes to know

  • Graduate visa: if you study in the UK and apply for the Graduate visa from 1 January 2027, you get 18 months instead of 2 years. PhD graduates still get 3 years.
  • Visa brake: the restrictions announced on 26 March 2026 apply to Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar and Sudan only.

How to apply

  1. Find a job with an employer that holds a UK sponsor licence. You can check any employer on the register of licensed sponsors.
  2. Your employer assigns you a certificate of sponsorship.
  3. Take an approved English test, such as IELTS for UKVI.
  4. Apply online on GOV.UK and attend your biometrics appointment.

Watch out for fees

Your employer must pay its own Immigration Skills Charge. GOV.UK warns sponsors that their licence may be revoked if they ask a sponsored worker to pay it or any costs linked to their application. Anyone asking you for money for a “certificate of sponsorship” is a red flag.
